findings.note: FALSE: "There is no AO2 for modern texts — you do not need to analyse language techniques." AO2 IS assessed on AQA 8702 Paper 2 Section A and is worth 12 of the 30 marks (AO1=12, AO2=12, AO3=6, plus 4 for AO4/SPaG). This is the first exam guidance a student meets in the unit.
findings.before: You are assessed on AO1 (argument and evidence), AO3 (context), and AO4 (spelling, punctuation, and grammar). There is no AO2 for modern texts — you do not need to analyse language techniques, but using relevant quotations to support your argument will strengthen your AO1.
findings.after: You are assessed on AO1 (argument and evidence, 12 marks), AO2 (Kelly’s methods and their effects, 12 marks), AO3 (context, 6 marks), and AO4 (spelling, punctuation, and grammar, 4 marks). AO2 carries exactly as many marks as AO1, so write about how Kelly builds the play — its four-act structure, its staging, its silences — as well as what it means.

findings.note: FALSE: "no AO2 for modern texts ... not language analysis". Same denial as L1, in the tip a student reads immediately before planning a character essay.
findings.before: Remember: no AO2 for modern texts — focus on what the character reveals about Kelly’s ideas, not on language analysis.
findings.after: Remember: AO2 is worth 12 of the 30 marks, so write about how Kelly builds the character — the lines he gives them, the moments he stages — as well as what the character reveals about his ideas.

findings.note: the lesson card summarised the whole lesson as "no AO2". Card text is what a student sees before opening the lesson.

findings.after: AQA modern text essay technique: no extract, AO1 and AO2 weighted equally, quotation strategies, model paragraph.

findings.note: vague hedge in board-specific AQA content, sitting in the same paragraph as the closed-book claim. Replaced with the actual AQA weightings, which is what makes the AO2 correction stick — otherwise the lesson still sends the student away to find out whether AO2 counts.
findings.before: Check your exam board’s specimen paper for the exact mark weightings and time allowance that apply to you.
findings.after: On AQA Paper 2 Section A the 30 marks are split AO1 12, AO2 12 and AO3 6, with a further 4 marks for spelling, punctuation and grammar.

findings.note: the Key Fact box ended "Close language analysis is usually not the focus of this question" and listed only three things, dropping the strand worth 12 marks. Methods added as the second thing; "three" becomes "four".
findings.before: A strong modern text essay on DNA delivers three things: a sustained, personal response to the play supported by references from memory; context (Milgram, 2008 youth violence, moral philosophy, Connections programme) embedded in your analysis; and clear, fluent academic writing. Close language analysis is usually not the focus of this question.
findings.after: A strong modern text essay on DNA delivers four things: a sustained, personal response to the play supported by references from memory; analysis of Kelly’s methods — the four-act structure, the staging, the silences — and the effects they create; context (Milgram, 2008 youth violence, moral philosophy, Connections programme) embedded in your analysis; and clear, fluent academic writing.

findings.note: the section "What Each Strand of Your Essay Needs to Do" listed exactly three strands — argument (AO1), context (AO3), writing quality (AO4) — which is the denial expressed as structure: a student who reads only this section still learns the wrong AO set. AO2 folded into the argument strand rather than inserted as a new narration block, so no manifest re-ordering is needed.
findings.before: Maintain an analytical style throughout — every paragraph should develop your reading of the play.
findings.after: Maintain an analytical style throughout — every paragraph should develop your reading of the play. Kelly’s methods are part of that argument: AO2 carries 12 marks, so say what his choices — the four-act structure, the silences, the field they keep returning to — actually do to an audience.

findings.note: the collapsible heading asserted the denial in the student's line of sight. Device-spotting really does earn nothing; AO2 analysis of the same choices earns up to 12 marks, and the heading now says which is which.
findings.before: Why Language-Technique Spotting Is Not the Focus
findings.after: Why Device-Spotting Is Not the Same as Analysis

findings.note: the body of that collapsible told students the focus is "what Kelly is saying ... rather than a technique checklist", i.e. that method analysis is optional. Rewritten to keep the true half (labels alone earn nothing) and drop the false half (methods are not the focus).
findings.before: Identifying language devices (“Kelly uses a metaphor…”) is usually not what earns marks on a modern text essay. You can, and should, discuss structural and dramatic choices — staging, silence, the four-act structure, the field as a recurring space — where they support your argument about Kelly’s ideas. But the focus is on what Kelly is saying (ideas, themes, context) rather than a technique checklist. Treat every structural observation as an opportunity to say more about meaning.
findings.after: Naming a device (“Kelly uses a metaphor…”) earns nothing on its own. AO2 rewards analysis of the effect a choice creates, so discuss Kelly’s structural and dramatic choices — staging, silence, the four-act structure, the field as a recurring space — and explain what each one does to an audience. Treat every observation about method as an opportunity to say more about meaning; a technique checklist with no meaning attached still earns nothing.

findings.after: Paper 2, Section A: one essay question on DNA, 30+4 marks, no extract. AO1 (12 marks) and AO2 (12 marks — Kelly’s methods) carry equal weight, with AO3 (6 marks) for context and AO4 (4 marks) for SPaG.
